finding.claim: A falsy key ('' or null) combined with a non-empty algorithms list disables signature verification, so unsigned tokens with an allowed alg are accepted.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token with alg in the operator's allowlist and an empty signature segment (decoder.js:24-43 accepts it).
finding.sink: Signature acceptance: verifier.js:274-280 and verifier.js:169 (skipped when signature is falsy).

trace.note: keyType check accepts 'string' and 'object', so '' and null pass.
'if (key && keyType !== function)' is false, so key preparation and the empty-key guard (verifier.js:38-40) are skipped.
hasKey = !!key is false.
hasKey && !signature is false, and the !hasKey && signature branch is false because signature is ''.
if (signature && ...) is skipped, so no verification happens.
alg is in allowedAlgorithms, so the token passes; claims are returned as verified.

finding.guards_checked: Empty-key guard at verifier.js:38-40 (bypassed); missing-signature check at verifier.js:274 (keyed on hasKey, false here); signature check at verifier.js:169 (keyed on truthiness). Async path is not affected: a returned '' key is rejected at verifier.js:464. With algorithms unset, allowedAlgorithms is [] and everything is rejected.

finding.claim: Non-TokenError results are cached as valid and later returned as a successful verification, so a previously rejected token is accepted on its second presentation.
finding.source: Validly signed token with an out-of-range date claim (e.g. nbf ~1e13 seconds, no iat). Requires the issuer to sign such claims.
finding.sink: Cache hit returns the cached Error as the payload: verifier.js:363-378 and handleCachedResult at verifier.js:141-157.

trace.note: new Date(adjusted).toISOString() throws RangeError for out-of-range dates.
throw cacheSet(cacheContext, e) for the RangeError.
cacheSet special-cases only TokenError; the RangeError falls to the valid-token branch with min=0 and max=now+cacheTTL when no iat is present.
Second call: cache hit passes since min===0 and max is in the future.
handleCachedResult: instanceof TokenError is false, so the RangeError is returned as the payload (sync) or as callback(null, error) (async).

finding.guards_checked: cacheSet TokenError-only branch (verifier.js:110); handleCachedResult type check (verifier.js:142). Neither covers non-TokenError errors. The first call does throw as intended.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, a Buffer token throws a TypeError from hashToken before decode converts it to a string.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token passed as a Buffer (verifier.js:353 accepts Buffer).
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) at verifier.js:364, calling utils.js:46 token.split('.', 1).

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) runs before decoder.js:14-15 converts the Buffer to a string.
hashToken calls token.split, which Buffer does not have, so a synchronous TypeError is thrown outside the callback path.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 accepts Buffer. decoder.js:14 conversion happens too late. No instanceof guard in the cache lookup.

finding.claim: Signature segments are malleable: non-canonical base64 trailing bits are accepted, contrary to the comment at verifier.js:166-168 that says the signature is canonical.
finding.source: Attacker mutates the trailing bits of a valid token's signature segment.
finding.sink: Signature decode at verifier.js:169 and crypto.js:297 (Buffer.from(signature, 'base64')).

trace.note: Only the base64url alphabet is checked, not canonical length or trailing bits.
Comment claims the signature is canonical by this point; this is false.
Node base64 decoding ignores unused trailing bits, so distinct strings decode to the same digest (4 variants for HS256). Not verified by execution.

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check at decoder.js:41. HMAC comparison at crypto.js:301 (timingSafeEqual) is correct, so forgery is not possible. Impact depends on app use of token strings for replay or revocation (not in repo).

finding.claim: errorCacheTTL caches a 'not yet valid' (FAST_JWT_INACTIVE) rejection past the token's nbf, because the error branch never sets a min bound.
finding.source: Token with a future nbf presented before it becomes valid (positive errorCacheTTL configured).
finding.sink: Cache hit at verifier.js:364-374 returns the cached inactive error after nbf has passed.

trace.note: TokenError branch sets max = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + ttl and leaves min=0.
The FAST_JWT_INACTIVE branch expects a min bound, which errors never get.
Cached rejection returned after nbf until errorCacheTTL expires.

finding.guards_checked: errorCacheTTL validation (verifier.js:551-559). Cache-hit range logic (verifier.js:368-375). Default errorCacheTTL is -1, which disables this.
